regex.lint.flag.y: Sticky (matches only at the current position)
regex.lint.err.unterminatedGroup: An opening ( isn't closed. Add the matching ), or write \( to match a literal parenthesis.
regex.lint.err.unmatchedParen: A closing ) has no matching opening parenthesis. Write \) to match a literal parenthesis.
regex.lint.err.nothingToRepeat: There's nothing before * + ? to repeat. To match a literal asterisk, plus or question mark, escape it: \* \+ \?
regex.lint.err.unterminatedClass: A [ isn't closed with ]. Write \[ to match a literal bracket.
regex.lint.err.rangeOrder: A range inside brackets is out of order (e.g. [z-a]). To use a literal hyphen, put it last or write \-.
regex.lint.err.numbersOrder: The numbers inside { } are out of order (e.g. {3,1}). Put the smaller one first.
regex.lint.err.groupName: The group name has invalid characters. Names in (?<name>…) can use only letters, digits and underscores, and can't start with a digit.
regex.lint.err.dupGroupName: The same group name appears twice. Names in (?<name>…) must be unique.
regex.lint.err.namedRef: No group matches \k<name>. Make the name exactly match (?<name>…).
regex.lint.err.invalidGroup: What follows (? is invalid. Allowed forms: (?:…) group only · (?=…) (?!…) lookahead · (?<=…) (?<!…) lookbehind · (?<name>…) named group.
regex.lint.err.brace: { } can't be read as a repeat count. Write \{ \} to match literal braces.
regex.lint.err.trailingBackslash: The pattern ends with a lone backslash (\). To match a literal backslash, write it twice: \\
regex.lint.err.escape: Invalid escape after a backslash. With the u · v flags, only defined escapes like \d \w \s \n \u{…} \p{…} are allowed.
regex.lint.err.classSet: Invalid expression inside brackets. With the v flag, symbols like ( ) [ ] { } / - | must be escaped with \.
regex.lint.err.tooLarge: The pattern is too large or too deep. Try splitting it into several scripts.
regex.lint.err.flags: Invalid flags. Only g i m s u y d v, each used once.
regex.lint.emptyFind: The find pattern is empty. Empty scripts don't run.
regex.lint.slashUnclosed: It starts with a slash but doesn't end as /pattern/flags, so the slash is searched for literally too. Check that you added the closing slash.
regex.lint.badFlags: Unsupported flags: {flags}. Supported flags are g i m s u y d v.
regex.lint.badFlagsForeign: Unsupported flags: {flags}. Supported flags are g i m s u y d v. (Flags from other regex engines don't work here.)
regex.lint.dupFlags: The same flag appears twice: {flags}. Use each only once.
regex.lint.uv: The u and v flags can't be used together. Keep just one.
regex.lint.markdownStar: If you're trying to match Markdown asterisks like *emphasis*, write \*([^*]+)\*.
regex.lint.noG: Without the g flag, only the first match is replaced. Add g at the end to replace all (e.g. /pattern/g).
regex.lint.nested: Repetition is nested inside repetition (near char {n}, e.g. (a+)+ or (.*)* ). Non-matching text can make the possibilities explode and freeze the screen. Narrow the inner repetition with something like [^…]+, or remove the outer one.
regex.lint.matchesEmpty: This pattern matches even with no characters. The replacement can end up between every character (or at every line start). If that's not intended, make it match at least one character, e.g. change * to + or drop the ?.
regex.lint.dotNewline: The dot (.) doesn't cross newlines. To match across lines, add the s flag or use [\s\S] instead of the dot.
regex.lint.anchorM: ^ and $ only mark the very start and end of the whole text. Add the m flag to match per line.
regex.lint.sticky: The y flag only matches at consecutive positions from the start of the text. You usually don't need it.
regex.lint.noTarget: No targets selected, so it won't run. Pick at least one, such as User input or AI output.
regex.lint.groupRef: Replace uses {refs}, but the find pattern only has {groups} capture groups. Those spots will be empty.
regex.lint.groupRefNone: Replace uses {refs}, but the find pattern only has {groups} capture groups. Those spots will be empty. Wrap the part you want in ( ).
regex.lint.namedMissing: Replace uses $<{name}>, but there's no named group (?<{name}>…) in the find pattern. That spot will be empty.
regex.lint.dollarSpecial: $& $` $' aren't supported and stay as literal text. Use {{match}} or $0 for the whole match.
regex.lint.trimNoCapture: Trim only removes text from parts pulled in with $1 · {{match}}. The current replacement doesn't pull in anything.
regex.lint.macroNoSubst: The find pattern has {{…}} macros, but "Macros in find" is set to "Don't substitute", so they're matched literally. Switch to "Insert raw" to match by name.
regex.lint.macroRaw: If a macro value contains symbols like . ( ) ?, they're read as regex syntax. Pick "Insert escaped" to match them literally.
regex.lint.depthOrder: Min depth ({min}) is greater than max depth ({max}), so it won't apply to any message.
regex.lint.depthStore: Depth is ignored when rewriting the original. It's only used for display and prompt.
regex.lint.loreMode: Lorebook content only passes through when sending to the AI. Set Apply to "Prompt only" or "Display + prompt" for it to affect the lorebook.
regex.lint.runOnEdit: "Also run on edit" only matters with "Rewrite the original". Display modes always reapply after edits.
regex.lint.why.multiline: The text spans multiple lines (the dot doesn't cross newlines)
regex.lint.why.anchor: ^ $ only mark the start and end of the whole text
regex.lint.why.curlyInText: The input uses curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), but the pattern looks for straight quotes (" ').
regex.lint.why.curlyInTextN: The input uses curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), but the pattern looks for straight quotes (" '). Accepting both, like ["“”], finds {count} matches.
regex.lint.why.curlyInPattern: The pattern looks for curly quotes (“ ”), but the input only has straight quotes (" ').
regex.lint.why.spaces: Spaces or line breaks differ from the pattern — using \s+ in place of spaces finds {count} matches.
regex.lint.why.partial: The start of the pattern, {head}, matches "{hit}", but it gets stuck after that at {rest}.
regex.lint.why.fromStart: Even the first part of the pattern doesn't match this input. Try pasting the input into the pattern as-is, then turn only the parts that vary into regex.

memoria.config.basic.title: Basics
memoria.config.basic.enabled.label: Use long-term memory
memoria.config.basic.enabled.hint: When off, both recording and injection stop.
memoria.config.basic.auto.label: Auto record
memoria.config.basic.auto.hint: Records a turn automatically whenever an AI reply finishes. When off, record manually with [Record now].
memoria.config.basic.supervisor.label: Scene director (experimental)
memoria.config.basic.supervisor.hint: After a reply, a director LLM briefly plans the next scene's goals and developments to avoid, and injects them into the next reply (1 extra call). Reply start isn't delayed.
memoria.config.basic.authorizePrivate.hi: Also uses inner thoughts and secrets within the scope chosen below. When off, only public memories are searched in every mode, including Novel / narrator.
memoria.config.basic.associative.label: Associative recall
memoria.config.basic.associative.hint: Adds up to 2 related memories as candidates via rare cues shared with directly found memories. Total recall count and token budget stay the same, and secret boundaries are respected. No extra API calls.
memoria.config.basic.autoHide.label: Auto-hide summarized messages
memoria.config.basic.autoHide.hintBefore: Old messages covered by the "Story so far" summary are
memoria.config.basic.autoHide.hintAfter: in the chat to save context tokens. They're hidden, not deleted — undo with "Show all hidden messages" in the Tools tab. Recent messages are always kept as set below.
memoria.config.basic.autoHide.done: Hid old messages covered by summaries. You can undo this anytime in the Tools tab.
memoria.config.basic.refProfile.label: Use card & persona
memoria.config.basic.refProfile.hint: The librarian and summaries use the character card and persona gist as background. Reduces mix-ups with names and settings.
memoria.config.basic.refLore.label: Use lorebooks
memoria.config.basic.refLore.hint: Uses active lorebooks as background. Large lorebooks increase librarian call tokens.
memoria.config.basic.audit.label: Learn from recall hits
memoria.config.basic.audit.hint: Checks whether injected memories were actually reflected in the reply and nudges their importance up or down slightly. Pinned and manual memories are left alone.
memoria.config.basic.trim.label: Don't send old, already recorded chat
memoria.config.basic.trim.hint: Messages aren't hidden; only when sending, the chat is trimmed to the "Recent messages to send" below.
memoria.config.basic.language.label: Summary language
memoria.config.basic.language.title: Language summaries and memories are written in
memoria.config.basic.summaryContextCount: How many previous summaries to reference when writing a new one (0 = none, -1 = all)
memoria.config.basic.preserveRecent.titl: With auto-hide on, how many recent messages to keep visible as original text
memoria.config.basic.recordDelay.label: Record delay (turns)
memoria.config.basic.recordDelay.title: Records only after the story has moved N more turns past the reply (0 = immediately)
memoria.config.basic.keepRecent.label: Recent messages to send
memoria.config.basic.keepRecent.title: With "Don't send old, already recorded chat" on, how many recent messages to send to the AI

memoria.config.track.title: Trackers
memoria.config.track.desc: When on, the librarian picks these out of the chat automatically, records them, and includes them in every turn's injection.
memoria.config.track.cast.label: Cast
memoria.config.track.cast.hint: Automatically records new characters' profiles and their relationships. (Managed in the World tab)
memoria.config.track.lockEdited.label: Auto-lock profiles you edit
memoria.config.track.lockEdited.hint: Editing a character card locks it automatically. The librarian can't change a locked card's name, age, job, looks, speech or traits; only relationships keep updating. (You can lock or unlock each card in the World tab)
memoria.config.track.milestones.label: Event timeline
memoria.config.track.milestones.hint: Records only decisive turning points — confessions, revealed identities, deaths, irreversible choices. (Managed in the Story tab)
memoria.config.track.items.label: Items
memoria.config.track.items.hint: Tracks owners and state of meaningful gifts and plot-relevant objects. (Managed in the World tab)
memoria.config.track.storyClock.label: Story clock
memoria.config.track.storyClock.hint: Tracks in-story elapsed time like "the next morning" or "3 years later". After a big time skip, earlier memories naturally recede into the past, and recall marks how long ago they were, like "~3mo ago".
memoria.config.model.title: Model (librarian API)
memoria.config.model.desc: The API the librarian uses to record and summarize memories. A cheap, fast model is recommended.
memoria.config.model.testEmpty: Empty reply. Check the model settings.
memoria.config.model.conn.label: Librarian connection
memoria.config.model.conn.title: Connection for memory recording and summary calls. URL, key and model are managed on the Connections screen
memoria.config.model.responseTokens.titl: Max tokens for librarian replies. Keep it generous so summaries and records don't get cut off (default 24000)
memoria.config.model.reasoningHeadroom.t: For reasoning models, 'thinking' tokens count against the output limit too. This adds headroom so replies aren't cut off.
memoria.config.model.note.t2: like Gemini Thinking or GPT o-series as the librarian, thinking tokens eat into the output limit and replies get cut off (
memoria.config.model.note.t3: ). If archive cleanup or summaries fail with "model response error", raise this to 12000–16000. It's only a cap, so you're billed for what's actually used. For non-thinking models you can set it to 0. (default 8000)
memoria.config.embed.title: Semantic search embeddings (optional)
memoria.config.embed.desc: Embeddings greatly improve recall accuracy and catch synonyms and paraphrases. On failure it falls back to built-in search automatically.
memoria.config.embed.mode.label: Embedding source
memoria.config.embed.conn.label: Embedding connection
memoria.config.embed.conn.title: Borrows this connection's URL and key (the embedding path is added automatically for the type)
memoria.config.embed.kind.label: Embedding type
memoria.config.embed.kind.title: Which embedding endpoint the connection uses. Auto picks based on the connection type
memoria.config.embed.floor.label: Similarity floor
memoria.config.embed.floor.title: Cosine values below this are treated as 'unrelated' and dropped. Score distributions differ by model, so lower it if recall is poor.
memoria.config.embed.floor.hint: 0.35–0.5 suits OpenAI models; 0.2–0.3 suits models with lower scores like bge or e5. Lower it if nothing is recalled, raise it if unrelated memories come along. (default 0.35)
memoria.config.embed.testEmpty: Empty embedding response. Check the connection/model.
memoria.config.embed.recalc.label: Recalculate
memoria.config.embed.recalc.title: Recalculates API embeddings for all existing memories. New memories are calculated automatically.
memoria.config.inject.title: Injection · Search
memoria.config.inject.tokenBudget.label: Injection token budget
memoria.config.inject.tokenBudget.title: Max tokens injected long-term memory may take up
memoria.config.inject.position.label: Injection position
memoria.config.inject.position.title: Where in the prompt to put the long-term memory ledger
memoria.config.inject.position.split: Split (plot up front, current scene in chat)
memoria.config.inject.depth.label: Injection depth
memoria.config.inject.depth.title: In-chat injection depth (0 = right before the last message). Values larger than the chat length go at the very start of the chat history.
memoria.config.inject.topK.label: Recall count
memoria.config.inject.topK.title: Memories to recall per turn
memoria.config.inject.chunkTurns.label: Summary interval (turns)
memoria.config.inject.chunkTurns.title: Summarize automatically every this many turns
memoria.config.inject.maxMemories.label: Max memories
memoria.config.inject.maxMemories.title: When exceeded, old low-importance memories are pruned first (pinned/manual excluded)
memoria.config.inject.consolidateEvery.t: Every N turns the librarian sweeps the archive: merges duplicates, removes noise, rebalances importance. 0 = off. Pinned and manual memories are left alone. Chunks about the same event are also regrouped and merged into arcs.
memoria.config.inject.arcConsolidateEver: Every N turns, reviews only existing arcs and re-merges ones that are truly the same event but split by timing. 0 = off. Completely separate from chunk regrouping (archive cleanup) and far more conservative.
memoria.config.inject.advanced: Advanced — recall score · plot threads · chronicle
memoria.config.inject.minScore.label: Min recall score
memoria.config.inject.minScore.title: Memories below this score aren't recalled
memoria.config.inject.minCosine.label: Min similarity
memoria.config.inject.minCosine.title: Cosine similarity floor for built-in search
memoria.config.inject.mmrLambda.label: Diversity (MMR λ)
memoria.config.inject.mmrLambda.title: Closer to 1 picks by score; lower picks more varied memories
memoria.config.inject.maxPerKind.label: Recalls per kind
memoria.config.inject.maxPerKind.title: Cap so one kind of memory doesn't take over recall
memoria.config.inject.maxPerTurn.label: Recalls per turn
memoria.config.inject.maxPerTurn.title: Cap so memories from one turn don't take over recall
memoria.config.inject.arcMergeAt.label: Chunk safety cap
memoria.config.inject.arcMergeAt.title: If chunks pile up past this count before archive cleanup, they're regrouped immediately
memoria.config.inject.threadSleepTurns.t: Plot threads with no progress for this many turns go to sleep (they stay in the archive and wake when mentioned again; 0 = off)
memoria.config.inject.eraKeep.label: Chronicles to keep
memoria.config.inject.eraKeep.title: Keeps up to this many chronicles separately; beyond that, the oldest are folded into one 'old story' (min 3)
memoria.config.inject.fossil.label: Turns until memories recede
memoria.config.inject.fossil.title: Memories older than this many turns recede into the past in recall

memoria.config.status.title: Status panel · Interludes · Checks
memoria.config.status.statusMode.label: Read status panel
memoria.config.status.statusMode.title: Reads the status panel attached to replies (time, date, place, weather) as-is, without calling a model
memoria.config.status.statusPattern.titl: A regex. The part captured in parentheses ( ) is read as the status panel
memoria.config.status.qrMode.label: QR messages
memoria.config.status.qrMode.title: Whether messages added via Quick Reply (QR) or commands are excluded from memory
memoria.config.status.sorter.label: Sort
memoria.config.status.sorter.title: Sort interludes — collect command messages and mark each as interlude or story
memoria.config.status.statusInject.label: Pass on the last status panel
memoria.config.status.statusInject.hint: Time, date and place carry over even when old replies are hidden or interludes come in between.
memoria.config.status.replyCheck.label: Continuity check
memoria.config.status.replyCheck.hint: Adds ⚠ next to the name when a new reply contradicts records or recent chat. Uses one more librarian API call per reply.
memoria.config.status.note: Interludes are QR results like quizzes, interviews or fortunes that pause the roleplay. If the instruction says to "stop the roleplay/scenario", they're detected automatically and left out of recording, recall and checks.
memoria.config.voice.title: Characters & voice
memoria.config.voice.desc: Summaries are written in a narrator's voice and old original text gets hidden, so as chats grow long, characters' voices blur and stale phrasing and tics come back. These settings prevent that.
memoria.config.voice.styleGuard.label: Ledger is for facts only
memoria.config.voice.styleGuard.hint: When injecting the ledger, adds: "Use the ledger only to check facts; follow the current chat's style and don't reuse old phrasing · follow characters' base personality and speech, and keep relationships at their current stage."
memoria.config.voice.recallQuotes.label: Include old original lines in recall
memoria.config.voice.recallQuotes.hint: When off, recall includes only summaries, no quoted old lines. Turn off if old speech patterns keep coming back.
memoria.config.voice.voiceSamples.label: Voice samples per scene character
memoria.config.voice.voiceSamples.title: For each character in the current scene, how many of their actual lines to include as voice samples (0 = none). Only lines found verbatim in the original text are used.
memoria.config.voice.banned.title: Banned · repeated phrases
memoria.config.voice.banned.ph: One per line, or comma-separated — e.g. softly, the corner of his lips twitched
memoria.config.voice.repeat.label: Tics
memoria.config.voice.repeat.title: Find verbal tics
memoria.config.voice.banned.hint: Listed phrases are removed from what long-term memory injects (memories, recall, summaries, quotes). Old lines containing banned phrases are dropped entirely.
memoria.config.voice.banned.hintBold: Don't add words the character always uses.
memoria.config.voice.banInChat.label: Also remove from recent chat sent to the AI
memoria.config.voice.banInChat.hint: Breaks the loop of the AI repeating itself after seeing its own recent replies. The saved chat is unchanged, and the last reply being continued is left alone.
memoria.config.voice.banTell.label: Tell the AI the banned phrase list
memoria.config.voice.banTell.hint: Tells the AI directly "don't use these phrases". Some models may be primed by the words instead, so it's off by default.
memoria.config.speed.title: Reply speed · Cache
memoria.config.speed.desc: Keeps long-term memory from slowing down replies. Reply generation always comes first.
memoria.config.speed.recallWaitSec.label: Max wait before reply (s)
memoria.config.speed.recallWaitSec.title: How many seconds to wait for the recall embedding response before generating. If exceeded, generates right away with built-in search results only. 0 = no limit
Rebuilds the fixed ledger every this many turns. 0 = only when changed lines pile up or entries are deleted
memoria.config.speed.yieldToChat.label: Replies first
memoria.config.speed.yieldToChat.hint: While a reply is generating, no new librarian or summary calls start; they resume after the reply arrives. Prevents replies from queueing when an API or proxy takes one request at a time.
memoria.config.speed.watchUpdates.label: Re-record messages changed by other features
memoria.config.speed.watchUpdates.hint: When a feature that rewrites replies or inserts translations or images changes a message, the turn is re-recorded only if the text actually changed. Nothing happens if only the display was redrawn.
memoria.config.speed.splitInjection.hint: Rarely changing parts of the ledger (canon, cast, relationships, summaries, pledges) are built once and kept at the front of the prompt; only per-turn parts (recall, current scene, status, lines changed since) go separately next to the recent chat. The prompt's front stays the same each turn, cutting cost and latency on models that support caching. The cache is rebuilt once on turns the fixed ledger refreshes, so it pays off most
when the position is "Before main prompt" or auto-hide is also on

scenebook.guide.step.engine.title: Choose an image engine
scenebook.guide.step.engine.body: Choose the image engine in Features › Illustration › Generate. For NovelAI, enter your key (Persistent API Token) and use the check button above to see your account status. NovelAI and proxied connections only work when Dreamland is opened through its server (start.bat).
scenebook.guide.step.cast.title: Register characters
scenebook.guide.step.cast.body: In the Cast tab, pick a save scope, then enter name, fixed appearance and default outfit. Global is the default for all chats, Current character applies to all of that character's chats, and Current chat applies only here. Appearance written in the Assets tab of the character or persona editor is merged in automatically. Appearance profiles are for alternate looks, like transformations or other outfits, and when they apply.
scenebook.guide.step.auto.title: Draw automatically
scenebook.guide.step.auto.body: Set automation at the top to Auto-generate and the model writing the reply adds an illustration plan at the end, which is drawn right away and attached below the reply. To review first, use Drafts only: scenes are saved and you can choose Draw or Edit scenes under the reply.
scenebook.guide.step.prompt.title: Prompts and placement
scenebook.guide.step.prompt.body: In Edit scenes, adjust the scene prompt, camera and negatives, and refine each character's prompt in Cast · placement. Drag the numbered dots or type coordinates to set positions. The up/down buttons change character order.
scenebook.guide.step.draw.title: Draw and revise
scenebook.guide.step.draw.body: Check what will actually be sent in the Prompt tab, then press Draw. The pencil button on an image edits the scene; the arrow button regenerates with a new seed. Revisions stack up as versions you can flip through with ‹ › at the bottom right. Click an image to view it large and edit, regenerate or save.
scenebook.guide.topic.format.title: Plan format · saving tokens
scenebook.guide.topic.format.body: The default prompt has the AI skip scene titles and answer in a short one-item-per-line format instead of JSON. This avoids bracket and quote errors and uses fewer tokens. Older JSON-format prompts still work; switch to the new format with Prompt › Injection › Default prompt. Turning on Generate › Prompt › Concise illustration prompt swaps in a short version about 1/5 the length for every reply. Turn it off if plans are often missing.
scenebook.guide.topic.framing.title: Camera · aspect ratio
scenebook.guide.topic.framing.body: The default prompt first picks an angle where the key action, faces and points of contact are actually visible: hugging or facing scenes from the side, lying together from above, someone walking away from behind. With Generate › Image › Switch portrait/landscape per scene on, the AI picks portrait, landscape or square for each scene, and you can change it in Edit scenes. Older saved injection prompts don't do this, so press Prompt › Injection › Default prompt to switch.
scenebook.guide.topic.quickEdit.title: Edit scene · regenerate
scenebook.guide.topic.quickEdit.body: Press the pencil on an illustration or Edit in the large view to open Edit scene. Describe what you want and press Rewrite with AI, or edit the camera buttons, aspect ratio, scene and character text yourself, then press Regenerate. The new image is added as a version in the same spot. Rewrite with AI sends one request over the analysis connection. Detailed edit opens Edit scenes, including character placement.
scenebook.guide.topic.frame.title: Illustration frames
scenebook.guide.topic.frame.body: Choose in Generate › Chat display › Illustration frame. Line-ornament frames such as Stars, Double line, Vine corners, Sprig and Art nouveau are drawn to fit the image, and their color can be white, black, gold, navy, wine or pink. Add frame image lets you add a PNG or WebP frame with a transparent center; its window position and shape are detected automatically. If you add separate portrait and landscape frames, set the landscape one for landscape images in its entry. Only the display changes; the original image is untouched.
scenebook.guide.topic.look.title: Art style · batch drafts
scenebook.guide.topic.look.body: Pick semi-realistic, watercolor, B&W manga, pixel art and more in Generate › Image › Art style to prepend those tags to the main prompt. Regenerating an existing image keeps the style recorded for it. Generate N drafts in the Jobs tab queues every reply that has a saved draft but no image.
scenebook.guide.topic.menu.title: Per-reply illustration menu
scenebook.guide.topic.menu.body: Press Edit scenes in a reply's ⋯ menu to open Edit scenes for that reply. You can illustrate older replies too. Editing a reply keeps its illustrations, scene drafts and plan log.
scenebook.guide.topic.automatic.title: Automation
scenebook.guide.topic.automatic.body: Off stops both plan instructions and auto-generation. Drafts only just saves scenes; Auto-generate draws and attaches images too. A reply interval of 2 handles every other reply.
scenebook.guide.topic.planMode.title: Planning mode
scenebook.guide.topic.planMode.body: Plan with reply receives the plan in a hidden comment (<!--scenebook … -->) at the end of the reply, with no extra call. The comment is stripped from the screen and later context. Separate analysis after reply asks once more over a secondary connection after the reply finishes.
scenebook.guide.topic.noPlan.title: When there's no plan
scenebook.guide.topic.noPlan.body: If the model skips the plan, a notice appears under the reply. Press Analyze scene to extract one separately, or check what was received in Jobs › Plan log. Slightly broken or cut-off JSON gets its commas, brackets and arrays repaired automatically.
scenebook.guide.topic.analysis.title: Analysis mode
scenebook.guide.topic.analysis.body: Fast extracts scenes directly. Precise first checks when characters' outfits changed, so it makes one more call.
scenebook.guide.topic.budget.title: Cost guard
scenebook.guide.topic.budget.body: Blocks NovelAI requests over 1,048,576 pixels or 28 steps. It doesn't check your subscription or balance, so it doesn't guarantee free generation.
scenebook.guide.topic.retry.title: Failures and retries
scenebook.guide.topic.retry.body: Paid requests that failed or couldn't be confirmed are never resent automatically. Key, balance, permission or rate-limit errors pause the queue. After a rate limit (429) it waits 60 seconds.
scenebook.guide.topic.seed.title: Seed
scenebook.guide.topic.seed.body: -1 means a new value each time. From an image's More menu you can redraw with the same seed or save it as the default seed. The same seed with a different model or settings gives a different image.
scenebook.guide.topic.placement.title: Cast · placement
scenebook.guide.topic.placement.body: Numbers follow character prompt order. V5 uses free coordinates; V4.5 snaps to the centers of a 5 × 5 grid. Arrow keys move too, and Shift moves further. Spread evenly, Flip horizontally and Center tidy things up quickly. Coordinates are a composition hint, not a guaranteed position.
scenebook.guide.topic.scope.title: Cast scope
scenebook.guide.topic.scope.body: Priority is Current chat → Current character → Global. The cast list, appearance profiles, world, direction and your-character settings are saved as one bundle; lists are not merged. For group chats, use the Global and Current chat scopes.
scenebook.guide.topic.refs.title: References: Vibe / Precise
scenebook.guide.topic.refs.body: In NovelAI V4.5, carries an image's mood or a character's features into new images. Vibe is for mood and art style, Precise for characters and style; adjust strength, fidelity and information extracted. Vibe makes one encoding request the first time it's used. Not available on V5.
scenebook.guide.topic.imageRead.title: Read image
scenebook.guide.topic.imageRead.body: Reads the main and UC prompts plus model, resolution, steps, CFG and sampler from an original NovelAI PNG. Apply to settings saves it as the shared style; Open as scene loads it into this scene without changing settings. Character prompts, coordinates and seed are not imported, and screenshots or converted copies can't be read.
scenebook.guide.topic.anchor.title: Insert position
scenebook.guide.topic.anchor.body: The default is below the reply. Switch to After paragraph in Generate › Chat display to pick a paragraph in Edit scenes; if the spot can't be found, the image goes below the reply.
scenebook.guide.topic.delete.title: Delete · hide illustrations
scenebook.guide.topic.delete.body: Hide or delete from an image's More menu. Deleting removes all versions in that spot from the chat, but the images stay in the gallery and can be added back. Deleting from the gallery removes them completely.
scenebook.guide.topic.queue.title: Jobs · gallery
scenebook.guide.topic.queue.body: Pause and resume apply from the next request; requests already sent aren't cancelled. The gallery searches illustrations from all chats by title or prompt; click one to add it to the current chat or reopen it as a scene.
scenebook.guide.topic.presets.title: Presets · backup
scenebook.guide.topic.presets.body: Save generation settings under a name and switch between them. Up to 10 previous settings are kept automatically and can be restored from Previous settings. Exported files never contain keys, and automation is turned off after importing.
scenebook.guide.topic.adult.title: Adult scene prompts
scenebook.guide.topic.adult.body: Only when the source text directly depicts explicit sexual activity between adults, the shared scene prompt gets the number of people, rating and the exact act or position, and each character prompt gets their role, pose, expression and state of dress, so they match. Acts not in the text are never added, and it doesn't apply to anyone not clearly an adult. See the full text in Prompt › Output rules.
scenebook.guide.topic.missing.title: Preventing missing plans
scenebook.guide.topic.missing.body: The prompt asks, at both start and end, for the reply body and the illustration plan to both appear in the final reply. It notes that a new reply needs a new plan even if earlier plans are hidden from history, and that writing it only in reasoning doesn't count. Each reply that's asked for a plan must include at least one image; empty plans are rejected. With no new action, it's told to use the established surroundings. If you don't need illustrations, turn off automation.
scenebook.guide.topic.where.title: Where the prompt goes
scenebook.guide.topic.where.body: The illustration plan prompt is appended at the very end, after the whole preset is assembled, wrapped in an <image_generation> tag. It isn't sent on replies outside the reply interval. View and edit it with the Prompt button at the top.
scenebook.guide.topic.saving.title: Saving · restoring settings
scenebook.guide.topic.saving.body: Settings save as you type. If you see Needs check or Not saved, fix the marked value. Generate › Presets · backup › Previous settings can restore up to 10 earlier versions.
scenebook.guide.topic.progress.title: Progress · failure notices
scenebook.guide.topic.progress.body: While drawing, a dashed placeholder sits under the reply, and images being redrawn are marked. You get a notice when done; on failure the reason is shown under the reply and in the Jobs tab and the gallery's Unfinished list. Failed paid requests are never resent automatically.
scenebook.guide.topic.share.title: Sharing prompts
scenebook.guide.topic.share.body: In Generate › Prompt › Edit · share, edit the shared style and negatives, the manual analysis prompt and the injection prompt, and exchange them as JSON files. Chat content and keys are never included. Export in Edit scenes saves the current scenes' prompts, characters and generation options.
scenebook.guide.topic.scopeCopy.title: Copying · clearing cast scope
scenebook.guide.topic.scopeCopy.body: Switching the save scope opens that scope's content. To use the character you're editing in another scope, press Copy; if settings already exist there, you'll be asked before overwriting. Use character settings / Use global settings clears this scope and follows the one above.
scenebook.guide.topic.refDelete.title: Deleting reference images
scenebook.guide.topic.refDelete.body: The trash button in the References tab deletes the image and removes it from the active list and presets. Queued jobs using it are cancelled; illustrations already drawn are kept. Older scenes that still point to it tell you when reopened and drop it.
scenebook.guide.topic.revise.title: Revise · drafts
scenebook.guide.topic.revise.body: Re-analyze passes your direction to the model; you can narrow it to camera, background or characters. Save draft lets you continue later, and closing with unsaved changes asks first. Undo returns to before the scene or cast list changed.
scenebook.guide.topic.review.title: AI review
scenebook.guide.topic.review.body: More › AI review on an image evaluates it over a vision-capable connection (the one used for manual analysis) and points out noticeable problems with characters, outfits, positions or composition. It's only advice and never changes the image or its versions. Results are also kept in the generation record.
scenebook.guide.topic.export.title: Export chat
scenebook.guide.topic.export.body: Gallery › More › Export current chat saves the visible illustrations and the chat as a single HTML file. If the insert position is after a paragraph, images go after that paragraph.
scenebook.guide.topic.model.title: Model
scenebook.guide.topic.model.body: The NovelAI model used to draw. V5 supports free coordinates; V4.5 supports 5 × 5 character placement and image references.
scenebook.guide.topic.size.title: Width · height
scenebook.guide.topic.size.body: The output image size in pixels. NovelAI uses multiples of 64. The size shown in chat is set separately by Max width.
scenebook.guide.topic.steps.title: Steps
scenebook.guide.topic.steps.body: How many denoising passes to run. Higher can take more time and cost, and isn't always better.
scenebook.guide.topic.guidance.title: Guidance
scenebook.guide.topic.guidance.body: How strongly the prompt is followed. Too high can overdo colors and outlines.
scenebook.guide.topic.sampler.title: Sampler · scheduler
scenebook.guide.topic.sampler.body: The method used to refine the image and how noise is reduced over steps. Changing them changes the result even with the same seed. V5 uses Karras.
scenebook.guide.topic.rescale.title: CFG rescale
scenebook.guide.topic.rescale.body: Softens brightness and contrast pushed too far by Guidance. 0 means off.
scenebook.guide.topic.quality.title: Quality tags
scenebook.guide.topic.quality.body: Adds model-specific quality tags after the style and scene. Turned off when importing a scene from an image, to avoid duplicates.
scenebook.guide.topic.order.title: Use coordinates · character order
scenebook.guide.topic.order.body: Use coordinates sends each character's position on screen; Use character order sends the order of character prompts. Change the order with the up/down buttons in Cast · placement.
scenebook.guide.topic.conn.title: Analysis connection
scenebook.guide.topic.conn.body: If none is chosen, the current chat's connection is used for analysis. This is separate from the image engine's key.
scenebook.guide.topic.maxScenes.title: Max scenes
scenebook.guide.topic.maxScenes.body: The most scenes to extract or draw from one reply. Usually one; more only when there are clearly different moments.
scenebook.guide.topic.context.title: Previous messages to read
scenebook.guide.topic.context.body: How many messages before the chosen reply are read. More means more is sent for analysis. Later messages are not read.
scenebook.guide.topic.style.title: Style · negatives
scenebook.guide.topic.style.body: Style is the shared prompt prepended to every image; negatives are things you don't want drawn. Shared, per-scene and per-character negatives apply separately, and Edit scenes can change the values for this job only.
scenebook.guide.topic.transparent.title: Transparent background
scenebook.guide.topic.transparent.body: Requests an image with an alpha channel on V5.
scenebook.guide.topic.display.title: Max width · small display
scenebook.guide.topic.display.body: How large illustrations appear in chat. The stored image resolution doesn't change.
scenebook.guide.topic.player.title: Drawing your character
scenebook.guide.topic.player.body: Don't draw keeps your character off-screen (POV). Only when in the reply draws them only when visible in the text; Always when present draws them whenever they're there in that moment.

settings.term.label: What to log in the server terminal (Termux, etc.)
settings.term.hint: Each model call is logged in the terminal running the server. Full prints the exact request sent to the provider (messages and settings) and the response, like SillyTavern; summary shows the connection, model and settings, one line per message, and the time, tokens and errors. API keys are never printed. After updating, restart the server once to get the new format.
